slot.brief: Use symmetry about the axis and the property ∫₀ᵃ f(x)dx with f(a−x) to evaluate a nontrivial definite integral without full antiderivatives.

verdicts.working: Let f(x) be the integrand. Then f(x)+f(π/2−x)=1, since the two numerators sum to the denominator. Hence 2I=π/2 and I=π/4.

working:
Let $f(x)$ be the integrand. Then $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-xight)$ has numerator $\cos^4x+2\sin^2x\cos^2x$.
$f(x)+f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-xight)=1$.
By reflection, $\int_0^{\pi/2} f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}-xight)dx=I$.
$2I=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\Rightarrow I=\dfrac{\pi}{4}$.

solution:
Let $f(x)$ denote the integrand. Under $x\mapsto \frac{\pi}{2}-x$, its numerator becomes $\cos^4x+2\sin^2x\cos^2x$; the two numerators sum to the denominator, so $f(x)+f\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-x\right)=1$.
By reflection, both integrals equal $I$, hence $$2I=\int_0^{\pi/2}1\,dx=\frac{\pi}{2}\quad\Rightarrow\quad I=\frac{\pi}{4}.$$
